answers.answer: Boat Attack is Unity-Technologies' Unity/Universal RP boat-racing demonstration and learning project: a small playable island-racing slice intended to support URP testing/development, explicitly supplied as-is. README credits Andre McGrail for design, programming, modeling, textures and SFX, Alex Best for modeling/textures, and Stintah for music. A developer/player runs it in Unity or a built player; no hosted service operator is evidenced.

Principal evidenced systems: RaceManager configures races, spawns boats, starts/ends races and ranks competitors; Boat owns each boat's setup, laps/checkpoints, appearance and camera/UI links; HumanController and AiController produce controls; BaseController resolves Boat/Engine references; Engine applies thrust/steering and samples water; InputControls provides action bindings; WaterSystem/GerstnerWavesJobs computes wave samples; RaceUI displays race state; AppSettings loads scenes and manages rendering settings. This is a source-backed overview, not an exhaustive subsystem inventory.

Gameplay is C# in Assets/Scripts, chiefly BoatAttack and BoatAttack.UI namespaces, using Unity MonoBehaviour lifecycle APIs. Rendering includes ShaderLab with HLSL; configuration/input definitions are JSON. ProjectVersion pins Unity 2020.3.23f1. Packages/manifest.json declares URP 10.7.0, Input System 1.1.1, Addressables 1.19.11, Cinemachine 2.9.1, Burst 1.4.11, Mathematics 1.2.5, UI/TMP and testing packages, plus an OpenUPM scope for gameplay ingredients. Embedded Packages/com.verasl.water-system is separately packaged as Water System 1.4.0-preview.1, with WaterSystem namespace and its own dependency declarations. Assembly-definition boundaries were not established.

For the selected human-boat path, RaceManager.SetGameType(Singleplayer) creates BoatData with human=true. SetHull selects its asset reference. LoadGame subscribes Setup to sceneLoaded; SetupRace creates boats. CreateBoats awaits Addressables.InstantiateAsync, obtains Boat and calls Setup(i+1, boat.human, livery). Boat.SetupController chooses typeof(HumanController) and dynamically AddComponent's it. HumanController.Awake creates bindings; OnEnable resolves the Engine through BaseController and enables BoatControls. Exact serialized menu-button dispatch and chosen prefab instance remain unverified.

Assets/Scripts/Boat/Engine.cs, Engine.Accelerate(float modifier), implements X. It acts only when cached _yHeight > -0.1f, clamps modifier to [0,1], flattens Rigidbody forward to horizontal and normalizes it, then AddForce(horsePower * modifier * forward, ForceMode.Acceleration), plus negative-right relative torque proportional to modifier. Engine.FixedUpdate samples the transformed enginePosition through GerstnerWavesJobs and computes _yHeight = sampled water y minus engine point y. Thus the precise gate tolerates a point up to just under 0.1 above sampled water; it is not simply a positive-depth test.

HumanController -> BaseController: inheritance and explicit base.OnEnable call. -> InputControls: construction, BoatControls/DebugControls subscriptions, enable/disable. -> Boat: inherited controller.ResetPosition(). -> Engine: inherited engine.Accelerate and Turn. -> DayNightController: SelectPreset(value). BaseController proves reference wiring via TryGetComponent<Boat> and controller.engine. InputAction callback dispatch points back into registered HumanController handlers; that is distinct from its outgoing dependency. Unity InputSystem, Time and Debug are external APIs, not additional internal components. DebugControls is subscribed here but not explicitly enabled here.

Holding a positive throttle binding produces BoatControls.Trottle performed input; its callback caches a float. Unity's FixedUpdate dispatch repeatedly calls HumanController.FixedUpdate, which passes the cached value to Engine.Accelerate; cancellation clears it. The engine's water gate, clamp and Rigidbody acceleration then apply. Boundaries: device/Input System event dispatch; dynamic AddComponent controller selection; inherited runtime Boat/Engine lookup; Unity lifecycle scheduling; wave-job sample production; and Unity physics integration. No direct synchronous callback-to-FixedUpdate edge exists, and relative ordering of the two components' FixedUpdate callbacks was not established.

Two direct consumers are evidenced: HumanController.FixedUpdate passes _throttle; AiController.FixedUpdate passes 1f when the target-direction dot product is positive, otherwise 0.25f, after checking for an available path point. Changed Engine.Accelerate semantics affect both. Boat, RaceManager and input bindings are upstream setup/data dependencies, not evidenced direct callers. Directory browsing failures prevented an exhaustive repository-wide caller claim.

README's documented examples are scenes/main_menu.unity for a complete play-through and scenes/demo_island.unity for a direct AI race; _levels/level_Island.unity is the level loaded from the menu. The supported human implementation entry is RaceManager's Singleplayer setup -> CreateBoats -> Boat.Setup -> HumanController -> Engine.Accelerate. The AI example has AiController.FixedUpdate -> Engine.Accelerate. README does not document a dedicated isolated acceleration test. The precise scene/prefab serialized callbacks connecting those examples to setup were not inspected, so the scene-to-code connection is partly inferred from documentation and implementation rather than runtime-proven.

Throttle enters through Assets/Data/InputControls.inputactions and its generated GameSystem/InputControls.cs wrapper, under the literal misspelling BoatControls.Trottle. A Value/Axis action uses AxisDeadzone(min=0.1,max=1). A 1DAxis composite maps left trigger/east button/down/S/Z negative and right trigger/south button/up/W/space positive; touchscreen touch-position Y is separately clamped [-1,1]. The wrapper creates an InputActionAsset from JSON and resolves that action. HumanController reads the performed float and resets on canceled; Engine finally clamps [0,1], so negative throttle cannot produce reverse thrust in this implementation.
